description.value: An fMRI study investigating neural mechanisms associated with visual cue-reactivity in frequent cannabis users in relation to quantitative levels and problem severity of cannabis use, comparing frequent users, sporadic users and cannabis-naive controls.

spans.text: The main goal of the current fMRI study was to investigate neural mechanisms associated with (visual) cue-reactivity in cannabis users in relation to quantitative levels and problem severity of cannabis use.

value: Within the group of frequent users, we expected levels of cannabis use and craving to correlate positively with activity in these brain structures.
Frequent users with a high-problem severity were expected to show increased activation in the dorsal striatum compared to frequent users with a low-problem severity.

description.value: Prospective fMRI study; participants were recruited from the Internet and cannabis outlets, and all participants signed informed consent prior to participation.

spans.text: The present study was part of a prospective fMRI study investigating the role of different neurocognitive and neuroimaging factors in the course of drug use in frequent cannabis users
The present study was part of a prospective fMRI study
Cue-reactivity was compared between frequent cannabis users, sporadic cannabis users and cannabis-naive healthy controls.
The medical ethics committee of the Academic Medical Centre of the University of Amsterdam approved the study and all participants signed informed consent prior to participation.
